title: What a business is — Quiz
objective: Identify the customer, offer, and delivery in a simple business example.

questions.prompt: Maya sells a $79 invoicing guide to freelance designers and sends buyers a download link. Which correctly identifies Customer → Offer → Delivery?

options.text: Freelance designers → the $79 invoicing guide → download link

questions.feedback: The customer buys, the offer specifies what they receive and its price, and delivery provides access to it.

retryScenario.prompt: Sam sells a $49 resume template to recent graduates and emails them a PDF. Which correctly identifies Customer → Offer → Delivery?

options.text: Recent graduates → the $49 resume template → emailed PDF

retryScenario.feedback: The customer buys, the offer specifies what they receive and its price, and delivery provides access to it.

questions.prompt: Leo builds an app. Friends praise it, but nobody has purchased access. What has he not yet demonstrated?

options.text: That he can build an app
That customers will actually pay for access

questions.feedback: Positive feedback demonstrates interest. It does not demonstrate completed purchases.

retryScenario.prompt: Nina posts free recipes. Followers leave glowing comments, but no one has bought her paid meal plan. What has she not yet demonstrated?

options.text: That customers will actually pay for the meal plan

retryScenario.feedback: Positive feedback demonstrates interest. It does not demonstrate completed purchases.

questions.prompt: A tutor identifies parents who want maths support and offers four lessons for $80, but has no way to schedule or conduct the lessons. Which part needs work?
questions.feedback: The customer and offer are specified. The tutor still needs a workable way to provide the promised lessons.

retryScenario.prompt: A coach identifies busy managers who want interview practice and offers a $120 session, but has no booking link or meeting setup. Which part needs work?
retryScenario.feedback: The customer and offer are specified. The coach still needs a workable way to provide the promised session.

applicationExercise.prompt: Name your customer, describe one offer with a price, and explain how you would deliver it.
applicationExercise.example: Busy freelancers buy my $79 invoicing guide and receive a download link.
applicationExercise.notes: Accept different valid answers; do not require exact wording.
